findings.title: Unguarded int() conversion on user-supplied cycle_budget in fallback mission creation path
findings.description: In dashboard_modules/core.py line 581, the fallback branch (when af_engine.mission_config is not importable) calls int(data.get('cycle_budget', 3)) with no try/except. A non-numeric value in the user-controlled JSON body raises an unhandled ValueError that results in a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a proper 400 Bad Request.
reproduction_steps: Ensure af_engine.mission_config is not importable (e.g., remove the module or simulate ImportError)
POST /api/mission with body: {"problem_statement": "test", "cycle_budget": "not-a-number"}
Observe unhandled ValueError traceback and 500 response
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the int() call in a try/except (ValueError, TypeError) and return a 400 response with a descriptive error message

findings.title: source_type query parameter not validated against allowlist before forwarding to storage
findings.description: In dashboard_modules/core.py line 721-725, the source_type query parameter from request.args is passed directly to storage.get_filtered() without route-level allowlist validation. The storage layer uses parameterized queries so SQL injection is blocked, but passing unknown enum values through to the DB layer silently returns empty results rather than a clear 400 error, and any future storage change could introduce a vulnerability.
reproduction_steps: GET /api/recommendations?source_type=arbitrary_unknown_value
Observe the request succeeds with 200 and empty items instead of a 400 validation error
findings.suggested_fix: Validate source_type_filter against a frozenset of allowed values ('drift_halt', 'successful_completion', 'merged', 'manual') before calling storage.get_filtered()

findings.title: Hardcoded user-specific allowed workspace roots make path validation non-portable
findings.description: _ALLOWED_WORKSPACE_ROOTS in blind_agent_runner.py is hardcoded to /home/vader/AI-AtlasForge paths. When deployed under any other user or directory, every call to launch_parallel_team() raises ValueError because no allowed root matches, making the entire red-team runner non-functional without modifying source code.
reproduction_steps: Deploy the application under a different username or to a different root directory
Call BlindAgentRedTeam().launch_parallel_team(workspace_dir=Path('/home/other/project').resolve(), ...)
Observe ValueError: workspace_dir is not within any allowed root
findings.suggested_fix: Derive allowed roots from configuration or from the application's detected installation directory at runtime rather than hardcoding /home/vader paths

findings.title: TOCTOU race between symlink check and file creation in parallel agent launch
findings.description: In blind_agent_runner.py lines 474-481, is_symlink() is called on results_file and findings_file, then open(..., 'w') is called to create them. These are not atomic: an attacker with filesystem access can insert a symlink between the check and the open, causing the open() to follow the symlink and truncate an arbitrary target file.
reproduction_steps: Run BlindAgentRedTeam.launch_parallel_team() against a workspace
Between the is_symlink() check (line 474) and open() call (line 478), create a symlink at the results_file path pointing to an arbitrary target (e.g., /etc/passwd)
Observe that open(..., 'w') truncates the symlink target
findings.suggested_fix: Use os.open() with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW flags (atomic creation that fails if the path exists or is a symlink) instead of the two-step check-then-open pattern

findings.title: Hardcoded error string prefixes for drift evaluator error detection miss non-standard error formats
findings.description: mission_drift_validator.py lines 568-570 detect evaluator errors only by checking three hardcoded string patterns. Any evaluator error string that does not match these exact prefixes (e.g., 'Error: network timeout', 'LLM error:', 'Timeout:') will set is_evaluation_error=False, causing the result to be counted as real drift and incrementing failure_count, potentially triggering a false HALT.
reproduction_steps: Configure the drift evaluator to return a response with evaluator_reasoning='Error: network timeout' and drift_detected=True with severity=HIGH
Observe that is_evaluation_error is False and failure_count is incremented as if real drift occurred
With enough such errors, consecutive_failures and failure_count thresholds can be falsely triggered
findings.suggested_fix: Use a broader error detection approach such as checking for common error prefixes with a tuple, or use a more flexible pattern like checking if evaluator_reasoning starts with any of several error-indicating keywords

findings.title: Bare except Exception in archival copy loop catches all exception types
findings.description: af_engine/core/archival.py line 558 catches bare Exception in the per-transcript copy loop, treating programming errors (TypeError, AttributeError) the same as expected I/O errors (OSError, shutil.Error), making debugging harder and potentially masking bugs.
reproduction_steps: Pass a non-Path object as a transcript to _parse_transcript_usage
Observe that the TypeError is caught and logged as a copy failure rather than propagating as a programming error
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the except clause to (OSError, shutil.Error) so that programming errors propagate as expected

findings.title: Silent except pass in stderr drain background thread
findings.description: In blind_agent_runner.py line 676, the _drain_stderr_bg inner function uses except Exception: pass, silently swallowing all errors from the background stderr drain thread. OSError or IOError on pipe read failures are discarded with no logging.
reproduction_steps: Close the subprocess stderr pipe while _drain_stderr_bg is reading
Observe that the resulting OSError is silently discarded with no log entry
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the bare pass with at minimum a logger.debug() call to log the exception type and message

findings.title: Silent except pass on stdout read in non-streaming agent path
findings.description: In blind_agent_runner.py lines 722-724, proc.stdout.read() on the non-streaming path uses except Exception: pass, so stdout read failures silently leave stdout_text as empty string with no log message, causing the agent to return no results with no indication of failure.
reproduction_steps: Close proc.stdout prematurely on the non-streaming code path
Observe the OSError is swallowed and the agent silently returns empty results
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the bare pass with at minimum a logger.warning() and set an error flag so the caller knows output was incomplete

findings.title: Duplicate independent allowlists for Claude start mode in core.py and dashboard_v2.py
findings.description: The mode allowlist for starting Claude appears independently in both dashboard_modules/core.py (line 281, inline set literal) and dashboard_v2.py (line 424, _ALLOWED_MODES). These are not linked, so updating one without the other silently creates inconsistency — a mode accepted by start_claude() could be rejected by the API route or vice versa.
reproduction_steps: Add a new mode 'experimental' to _ALLOWED_MODES in dashboard_v2.py
POST /api/start/experimental — the route rejects it with 400 because the inline check in core.py still only contains {"rd", "free"}
findings.suggested_fix: Import and reference the single _ALLOWED_MODES constant from dashboard_v2.py in the core.py route instead of duplicating it

findings.title: Rollback error not chained onto re-raised original exception in _get_connection
findings.description: In suggestion_storage.py lines 128-132, when rollback fails during exception handling, the rollback error is logged but not chained onto the re-raised exception. This means the exception traceback does not contain information about the rollback failure, making simultaneous DB-error + rollback-error scenarios hard to diagnose.
reproduction_steps: Trigger a DB operation error and then make conn.rollback() also fail
Observe that the exception chain only shows the original DB error, not the rollback error
findings.suggested_fix: Use `raise` after logging or use ExceptionGroup / chained exception for Python 3.11+ to preserve both errors in the traceback
